effects: The signer sends msg.value of ETH to the vault (VaultEthStaking.deposit -> _deposit(receiver, msg.value, referrer)).
The vault mints vault shares, worth the deposited ETH, to `receiver`, which can be any address (_mintShares(to, shares)).
The referrer is only written to the Deposited event and moves no assets.
formats.shown: "Stake ETH with p2p" with the receiver as 'Client address', the referrer, and the ETH value as 'Amount to deposit'.

findings.title: deposit labels the share receiver 'Client address' and does not say the stake goes to it.
findings.evidence: VaultEnterExit._deposit: `_mintShares(to, shares);` with to = receiver. Descriptor: `"label": "Client address", "path": "#.receiver"`. A receiver other than the signer gets the whole position.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "Shares receiver" (or "Stake owner") and add an interpolatedIntent such as "Stake {@.value} for {receiver}".

findings.title: deposit does not show how many vault shares the receiver gets; the code computes them from storage.
findings.evidence: VaultEnterExit._deposit: `shares = _convertToShares(assets, Math.Rounding.Ceil);` uses _totalShares and _totalAssets from storage.

cases.notes: Signer sent 0.01 ETH to the vault; screen shows 0.01 ETH. Receiver was the signer. Vault shares are internal balances, so no token event exists.

formats.key: updateStateAndDeposit(address receiver, address referrer, (bytes32 rewardsRoot, int160 reward, uint160 unlockedMevReward, bytes32[] proof) harvestParams)
effects: The call first harvests vault rewards with the keeper proof (updateState(harvestParams)), which changes the share price for all holders.
The signer sends msg.value of ETH to the vault.
The vault mints vault shares to `receiver`, which can be any address.
formats.shown: "Stake ETH with p2p" with the receiver as 'Client address', the referrer, and the ETH value as 'Amount to deposit'; the harvest params are hidden.

findings.title: updateStateAndDeposit labels the share receiver 'Client address' and does not say the stake goes to it.
findings.evidence: VaultEthStaking.updateStateAndDeposit -> deposit(receiver, referrer) -> _mintShares(to, shares). Descriptor: `"label": "Client address", "path": "#.receiver"`.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "Shares receiver" and add an interpolatedIntent such as "Stake {@.value} for {receiver}".

findings.title: updateStateAndDeposit does not show the minted share amount; it depends on storage and the harvest.

cases.notes: Not mined (chain 560048 cannot be read). From code: 0.1 ETH out is shown; shares go to the receiver shown as 'Client address'.

formats.key: claimExitedAssets(uint256 positionTicket, uint256 timestamp, uint256 exitQueueIndex)
effects: The vault sends the processed exited ETH of the signer's exit request to the signer (msg.sender) (_transferVaultAssets(msg.sender, exitedAssets)).
The signer's exit request is deleted. If only part was processed, a new request with the remaining tickets is created at a new position ticket.
formats.shown: "Claim exited assets" with the exit request timestamp as 'Exit initiated at'.

findings.title: claimExitedAssets does not show the ETH amount received; the exit queue in storage decides it.
findings.evidence: VaultEnterExit.claimExitedAssets: `(uint256 leftTickets, uint256 exitedTickets, uint256 exitedAssets) = calculateExitedAssets(msg.sender, positionTicket, timestamp, exitQueueIndex);` then `_transferVaultAssets(msg.sender, exitedAssets);`.

findings.title: claimExitedAssets intent does not name ETH or say the claim can be partial.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Claim exited assets". VaultEnterExit.claimExitedAssets: `if (leftTickets > 1) { newPositionTicket = positionTicket + exitedTickets; ... }` keeps the rest in the queue.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Claim unstaked ETH from p2p".

cases.notes: Not mined (chain 560048 cannot be read). From code: the signer receives ETH, and the screen gives no amount.

effects: The call takes `shares` vault shares from the signer's balance (_balances[user] -= shares, or _burnShares when the vault is not collateralized).
If the vault is collateralized, the call creates an exit request keyed to `receiver`. Only `receiver` can later claim the ETH with claimExitedAssets.
If the vault is not collateralized, the vault sends the ETH value of the shares to `receiver` at once.
The call reverts if the signer's osToken position LTV becomes too low (view check only).
formats.shown: "Exit funds" with 'Shares to exit' (18 decimals, unit 'shares') and the receiver as 'Client address'.

findings.title: enterExitQueue labels the ETH receiver 'Client address'; it does not say this address gets the ETH.
findings.evidence: VaultEnterExit._enterExitQueue: `_exitRequests[keccak256(abi.encode(receiver, block.timestamp, positionTicket))] = shares;` and `_transferVaultAssets(receiver, assets);`. claimExitedAssets keys on msg.sender. Descriptor: `"label": "Client address", "path": "#.receiver"`.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "ETH receiver" and add an interpolatedIntent such as "Unstake {shares} shares, ETH to {receiver}".

findings.title: enterExitQueue intent 'Exit funds' does not say it queues an unstake of vault shares for ETH.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Exit funds". VaultEnterExit._enterExitQueue puts the shares in the exit queue: `_queuedShares = SafeCast.toUint128(queuedShares + shares);`.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Request ETH unstake from p2p".

findings.title: enterExitQueue does not show the ETH value of the shares; the share price comes from storage.
